newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan short-lists eight bids for sugar tender.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan short-lists eight bids for sugar tender.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said on Monday it had short-listed eight bids for the import of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white refined sugar.
"We have short-listed eight bids and have sent them to the Commerce Ministry for final approval," said a TCP official, who asked not to be identified.
The TCP had invited tenders on May 12 from international suppliers for the import of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white refined sugar to be delivered in two equal shipments by June 30 and July 15.
He said the lowest bid for June 30 shipment was at $354 per tonne while the lowest bid for July 15 was at $334.50 per tonne. Both the bids were for Brazilian sugar, he added.
Final ministry approval for the tender may take a few days, he added.

The TCP says sugar imports were planned for the June and July period to control rising domestic prices and cover an expected shortage during the July-September period when the sugar crushing season ends.
